frequency_question: What proportion of complex bilateral water treaty renewals are fully negotiated, drafted, vetted, and formally signed within a 92-day calendar window?
membership_rule: Includes all formal negotiations for the renewal or succession of expiring international transboundary water treaties where the duration from initiation of final successor talks to formal signing was recorded; excludes domestic water agreements.

cases.name: US-Canada Columbia River Treaty regime updates and subsidiary negotiations
India-Pakistan Indus Waters Treaty permanent commissioner talks and modifications
Hungary-Slovakia Gabčíkovo–Nagymaros project dispute resolution and protocol adjustments
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase updates

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: Universal base rate for completing such a multi-step international legal harmonization process within 92 days is structurally zero based on the minimum physical time required for bureaucratic and technical processing.
known_gaps: Exact duration logs for minor memorandum of understanding renewals lacking public transparency.
skeleton: Comprehensive interstate water treaty negotiations requiring hydrological data harmonization, joint technical committee drafting, cabinet approvals, and legal vetting.
multiplier: Estimated minimum necessary sequential bureaucratic and technical steps: 1) Joint technical committee review (30 days); 2) Legal drafting and harmonization of texts (30 days); 3) Inter-ministerial consultation and bureaucratic clearance (30 days); 4) Cabinet-level formal authorization and scheduling signing ceremony (15 days). Total minimum physical duration = 105 days.
validity_reason: Bureaucratic drafting speeds and inter-ministerial clearance protocols change slowly over decades.
